kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA margin as a percentage of revenue, a key measure of operating profitability.
kpis.description: The adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 14.2% in 2025, an increase of 40 basis points compared to 13.8% in 2024, reflecting a structural improvement of 370 basis points since 2022 (10.7%). This improvement results from pricing discipline, a SG&A efficiency program delivering EUR 200 million in gross cost reductions, and an industrial excellence program including six site closures.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue in millions of euros for the 2025 fiscal year.
kpis.description: Revenue amounts to EUR 10.158 billion in 2025, down 5.2% compared to EUR 10.711 billion in 2024, reflecting soft market conditions and geopolitical challenges. The decline is mitigated by sustained pricing discipline and effective cost management.
kpis.signal: Market pressure contained by operational efficiency

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA in millions of euros, a measure of operational cash flow generation capability.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA amounts to EUR 1.444 billion in 2025, down 2.3% compared to EUR 1.478 billion in 2024, but up 24.8% since 2022 (EUR 1.157 billion), demonstrating the impact of structural margin improvement on value creation despite adverse market conditions.
kpis.signal: Stability in operational value creation despite revenue decline

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Operating income in millions of euros for the 2025 fiscal year.
kpis.description: Operating income reaches EUR 1.164 billion in 2025, reflecting strong operational performance driven by the execution of SG&A efficiency and industrial excellence programs, despite geopolitical challenges, tariffs, and currency impacts.
kpis.signal: Robust operating profitability in a challenging market environment

kpis.name: Employees (FTE)
kpis.explanation: Total number of full-time equivalent employees at AkzoNobel in 2025.
kpis.description: AkzoNobel employs 31,500 full-time equivalents in 2025, operating across more than 150 countries to support a world-class brand portfolio including Dulux, International, Sikkens, and Interpon.
kpis.signal: Global talent team spanning over 150 countries

kpis.name: Carbon Reduction S1&2
kpis.explanation: Percentage reduction in carbon footprint (scopes 1 and 2) compared to the 2018 baseline.
kpis.description: AkzoNobel has reduced its carbon footprint (scopes 1 and 2) by 47% compared to the 2018 baseline, up from 41% in 2024, demonstrating continued progress in decarbonization. This improvement reflects investments in renewable energy, including a EUR 50 million upgrade of the aerospace plant in Waukegan and the adoption of wind and solar power.
kpis.signal: Sustainability leadership with consistent annual progress toward climate goals

kpis.name: Return on Investment (ROI)
kpis.explanation: Return on investment measured as a percentage for the year 2025.
kpis.description: Return on investment reaches 13.5% in 2025, reflecting structural operational improvement and dynamic portfolio management, including the divestment of Akzo Nobel India Limited at 25x EBITDA and continued optimization of the decorative paints positioning in Southeast Asia.
kpis.signal: Capital efficiency reflecting operational improvement and portfolio management

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Earnings per share in euros for the 2025 fiscal year.
kpis.description: Earnings per share amount to EUR 3.71 in 2025, reflecting strong operational performance and improved profitability despite a challenging market environment.
kpis.signal: Sustained shareholder value creation driven by improved profitability

kpis.name: DPS
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of EUR 1.54 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Cap Return
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of EUR 0.382 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Proportion of net income distributed as dividends: 60.2% in the latest year.

risks.title: Goodwill and Decorative Brands Impairment Risk in China and North Asia
risks.score_rationale: Identified as a new Key Audit Matter in 2025, with €408M of assets involved; strong language ('historical revenue trends', 'significant management judgment', major organizational transition); deteriorating trend in historical DP CNA revenues; high-impact balance sheet category.

risks.title: Major Litigation Project Ichthys: €300M Provision Potentially Insufficient
risks.score_rationale: New Key Audit Matter in 2025 with a €300M provision booked in Q3 2025 and additional unprovided contingent liabilities; very strong language ('can be significant for the Group's financial statements as a whole', 'specialized legal expertise'); risk significantly increased; potential financial impact possibly exceeding the provisioned amount.

risks.title: Risk of Fraud and Circumvention of Internal Controls by Management
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned as a priority audit risk in the auditor's report; moderate but structural language ('management is in a unique position to perpetrate fraud'); stable and recurring risk in large multinationals; potential impact on the group's financial credibility.

risks.title: Risk of Fraudulent Revenue Recognition Linked to Growth Strategy
risks.score_rationale: Identified as a specific fraud risk related to AkzoNobel's growth and market share expansion strategy; direct language ('strategy to continuously grow and expand market share'); stable risk; impact on the reliability of published financial statements.

risks.title: Defined Benefit Pension Obligations: €7.7 Billion Exposure in the UK
risks.score_rationale: Recurring Key Audit Matter with a DB0 of €7.7B (ICI Pension Fund and Akzo Nobel CPS Scheme representing 89% of total); high sensitivity to actuarial assumptions (discount rates, inflation, longevity); stable trend but massive structural exposure; high-impact balance sheet category.

risks.title: Recoverability of Deferred Tax Assets in the Netherlands and the UK
risks.score_rationale: Key Audit Matter involving €224M in tax credits and €179M in tax loss carryforwards; high complexity due to local tax rules (interest limitations, specific credits); stable trend; dependence on future profit projections and tax planning strategies.

risks.title: Structural Reorganization of Decoratives: Execution and Transition Risks
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in the context of the DP CNA impairment test as an aggravating factor in 2025 ('transition to a new, more centralized organizational structure for the global Decorative Paints business'); newly identified risk; direct impact on asset valuation and operational performance; increasing trend.

risks.title: Multiple Legal Proceedings with Governments and Environmental Authorities
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in the context of Project Ichthys ('legal proceedings, as well as proceedings by/discussions with, governments, tax authorities, environmental agencies'); moderate language but multi-jurisdictional exposure; stable to upward trend due to strengthening global environmental regulation; potential impact on reputation and finances.
